hook:
Experience.

Every rival answered more power with all-wheel drive. Honda kept solving the harder problem.
body:
A limited-slip differential, a rev-match you can switch off, and suspension tuned at the Nürburgring. Still three pedals. Still no substitute.

2025 Honda Civic Type R FL5 — 315 hp · 310 lb-ft · 0–60 mph in 5.0 sec.

· 315 hp through the front axle alone, held by a helical limited-slip differential.
· Dual-axis front struts separate steering from suspension load, which is why the power does not tug at the wheel.
· 169 mph and 5.0 seconds to 60 mph, with three pedals and no automatic offered.
· Damping developed at the Nürburgring, and a rev-match you are allowed to switch off.

It remains the reference point for front-wheel-drive chassis engineering.
cta: Has front-wheel drive hit its ceiling, or has Honda just raised it again?
